transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been… losing my temper at work. Snapping at people. There was a safety meeting where I started yelling before I could stop myself, and now some of the younger inspectors seem scared to even ask me things.
Have you always had a tendency to lose your temper, or is this a relatively new development for you?

It’s… more of a new thing. I mean, I’ve gotten irritated before like anyone, but not like this. Lately I keep snapping, and that safety meeting—I was yelling before I even caught myself. Now some of the younger inspectors act nervous around me.
Do you find yourself acting on impulse more often lately, aside from just losing your temper?
I don’t know. I haven’t really thought of it that way. Mostly it’s just the snapping that people are noticing.
Have you been acting on impulse more often lately?
I’m not really sure. I guess I haven’t noticed doing things on impulse, besides… you know, the snapping.
Have you been doing things without thinking them through outside of work?
Outside of work? I… I don’t think so. Nothing that really stands out to me. Mostly people just say I get short with them.
Do you have recurring thoughts or ideas that you can't stop thinking about?

Yeah… sometimes. It’s not like an idea exactly. More like… a sound or smell sets it off. A cart clanks, or I smell hot oil, and I’m right back in that bay, seeing my coworker by the machine like it’s happening again.
Do these memories or thoughts cause you significant distress?
Yes… it does. When a cart clanks or I smell hot oil, it’s like I’m right back there in the bay, seeing him by the machine again. It’s… hard to shake.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places or activities because they remind you of the incident with your coworker?

Yeah… I do. I try not to go anywhere near the inspection bay if I can help it. And I don’t really talk about what happened. I used to go to those industrial-history talks, but I stopped… the pictures of the old machines just set me off.
Do you experience any physical symptoms when these memories come back to you?
I… I’m not really sure. I don’t pay much attention to what my body’s doing. I just know I feel off and want it to stop.
Do you often find yourself being easily startled by small noises or movements?

Yes… I guess I am. Even in the break room, or at rehearsal, I’m watching the doors and listening for any sudden machine noise. If someone moves behind me, I’m checking before I even think about it. It’s like my body won’t accept that I’m safe.
Do you often feel like you're constantly on the lookout for potential dangers?

Yeah… pretty much. Even in the break room, or at rehearsal, I catch myself watching the doors, listening for any sudden machine noise. If someone moves behind me, I check before I even think. It’s like… my body just doesn’t believe I’m safe.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms?
Since the machinery accident… after they changed me to the overnight schedule. So… about two years and four months, I guess.
Are there any specific activities or things you used to enjoy that you've stopped doing because they remind you of the accident?

Yes. I… avoid the inspection bay if I can. I’ll take the long way around.

And I don’t really talk about what happened. I used to go to those industrial-history talks sometimes, but I stopped. The old machinery photos… they’re too much.
Do you feel guilty or responsible in any way for what happened to your coworker in the machinery accident?
Yeah… I do. I keep going over it, thinking maybe if I’d pushed harder about the safety checks… or stopped that run when it didn’t feel right… maybe he wouldn’t have gotten hurt so bad.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?
I’m… not really sure. Some things, maybe. I don’t think about it much.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy since the accident?
I don’t know… maybe some. I just don’t really do as much anymore. It’s hard to tell.
Do you often feel worthless or that you're to blame for things that aren't your fault?
Yeah… I guess I do. I keep thinking if I’d pushed harder on the safety checks, or stopped that run when it felt wrong… maybe he wouldn’t have gotten hurt so bad.
Have you had difficulty performing your job or maintaining relationships with others since the accident?

Yeah… I’ve had trouble. I’ve missed a lot of shifts, and at work I don’t have much patience with the newer inspectors anymore. They don’t really trust me to mentor them now.

And… I stopped doing community theater mostly. I can’t count on myself to get through rehearsals.
